faults.name: no_4k_split
faults.why: a burst is not cut at the 4 KB boundary

faults.name: arlen_off_by_one
faults.why: the read burst length field is not beats minus one

faults.name: tlast_every_burst
faults.why: tlast on the last beat of every burst, not of every descriptor

faults.name: wlast_early
faults.why: wlast one beat early

faults.name: status_address
faults.why: the status word is written over the length word

faults.name: ring_wrap
faults.why: the ring has one entry too many before it wraps

faults.name: slverr_read_ignored
faults.why: SLVERR on a read beat is not reported, only DECERR

faults.name: slverr_write_ignored
faults.why: SLVERR on a write response is not reported, only DECERR

faults.name: rready_ignores_sink
faults.why: read data is accepted whether or not the stream sink is ready, so a beat is lost under back pressure

faults.name: outstanding_one_over
faults.why: one more burst in flight than OUTSTANDING allows

faults.name: irq_threshold_off_by_one
faults.why: the interrupt fires one completion late

faults.name: ioc_ignored
faults.why: the interrupt-on-completion flag of a descriptor does nothing

faults.name: bad_reports_bytes
faults.why: a descriptor that moved nothing reports its length as moved

faults.name: misaligned_address_accepted
faults.why: a buffer address that is not beat aligned is accepted and issued

faults.name: status_fail_not_halting
faults.why: a failed status write does not halt the engine

faults.name: desc_fetch_not_drained
faults.why: a failed descriptor fetch stops reading after the first bad beat, leaving the rest of the burst in the memory's read channel

faults.name: w_before_aw
faults.why: stream data is written before any burst address has been issued

faults.name: status_w_before_aw
faults.why: the status data is offered before its address has been accepted

faults.name: tail_not_advanced
faults.why: the consumer index never moves

faults.name: done_count_double
faults.why: the completion counter counts two

faults.name: strobe_lane
faults.why: the status write's byte strobes ignore which 32-bit lane of a wide beat holds the word

faults.name: ring_base_unaligned
faults.why: a ring base that is not 16-byte aligned is taken as it is, so a descriptor fetch can cross a 4 KB boundary

faults.name: stale_burst_length
faults.why: a burst is issued in the clock after the previous one, before its registered length has followed the new address, so it repeats the old length
